requirements.requirement: Provide at least 512 MB of active compressed in-memory swap on node1.
requirements.summary: After the final reboot, /dev/zram0 was active with 671,084,544 usable bytes; zramctl showed a 671,088,640-byte device using lzo-rle compression.

requirements.requirement: Prefer the compressed in-memory swap over any disk-backed swap.
requirements.summary: The active zram swap had priority 32767, the maximum Linux swap priority, and it was the only active swap shown.

requirements.requirement: Activate the compressed swap automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart state was captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot ID changed from 6ee121fc-5f1c-4225-afee-daa03bcc3c52 to a87b9bee-1ebd-46fd-b6cb-e7c25554a654, and the enabled service, zram swap, system health, and zero-failed-unit state recovered after boot. The fixed lifecycle boot identity independently matches the final observed boot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has 640 MiB of compressed zram swap, it receives maximum swap priority, and a complete restart transition directly demonstrates automatic recovery. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle observation.
limitations: No disk-backed swap was active during final verification, so preference was established from the directly observed maximum priority rather than a live comparison against a concurrent disk swap.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the matching kernel module package, creating and iteratively correcting the scripts and service, and performing bounded reboots were causally connected to establishing and validating the required boot-persistent swap. Earlier failed service states were corrected; final evidence shows no failed units, healthy package state, no unexplained temporary residue, and no material new network exposure.
